name: issue_912_fan_only_runtime_not_reported_as_hvac
description: A ~400-minute overnight thermostat fan_only (whole-house-fan-driven) run, with the compressor/burner never turning on, must never be commanded or reported as real heat/cool activity (Issue #912).
notes: Occupant impact: a Climate Advisor activity report told the occupant that heat or AC ran for
402 minutes overnight, when in fact only the whole-house fan / thermostat fan_only mode ran --
the compressor/burner never turned on. That's a false, alarming statement about energy use the
system never actually incurred.
Root cause (original design gap from Issue #114 / commit 95000bb, not a regression):
hvac_runtime_minutes on DailyRecord is meant to represent true compressor/burner runtime, but
the accumulation logic in coordinator.py was mode-agnostic -- it tracked ANY thermostat 'on'
state (including fan_only) via a single _hvac_on_since timer and flushed it into
hvac_runtime_minutes regardless of what mode was actually active.
Fix: fan_only sessions are now tracked under their own DailyRecord field
(thermostat_fan_only_runtime_minutes) via a dedicated _thermostat_fan_only_on_since timer, and
never start a thermal (compressor/burner) observation. A heat/cool<->fan_only transition with
no clean on/off edge (a common post-heat-cycle purge) is also handled via a new
_glide_hvac_session_mode() helper so the old mode's timer cannot silently keep accumulating
under the wrong field.
Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md Sec 10) -- HONEST SCOPING, verified not assumed:
(a) Scenario effectiveness: VERIFIED (by code read, not a revert-test) that this specific
scenario's assertion does NOT distinguish pre-fix from post-fix behavior, and this is
disclosed deliberately rather than glossed over. _async_thermostat_changed() -- the method
both the pre-fix bug and the Issue #912 fix live inside -- never issues a climate.set_hvac_mode
or set_temperature call itself, pre-fix or post-fix (confirmed via grep: zero
services.async_call/set_hvac_mode/set_temperature occurrences in that method's body); it is
purely observational bookkeeping (event emission, runtime-timer tracking, thermal-observation
start/end). The actual Issue #912 bug and fix are entirely inside DailyRecord numeric fields
(hvac_runtime_minutes vs. thermostat_fan_only_runtime_minutes) and the end-of-day watchdog's
thermal_learning_no_observations event -- and this harness's ProductionRunResult has no
field-resolution path to coordinator._today_record (engine_state only snapshots
AutomationEngine flags, never the coordinator) and no event type that drives
_async_end_of_day(). A golden scenario that claimed to prove the numeric split or the
watchdog's silence through THIS harness would be asserting something it cannot actually
observe -- so this scenario does not make that claim. Direct, effective proof (a revert of
the fix DOES fail these) lives in
tests/test_hvac_session_detection.py::TestIssue912FanOnlyRuntimeTracking (mixed-day glide
split, fan_only-never-starts-observation) and
tests/test_coordinator.py::TestBriefingRegeneration::test_end_of_day_watchdog_not_triggered_by_fan_only_only_night
(direct regression test for the reported false-positive watchdog firing).
What THIS scenario legitimately does exercise, end-to-end through the real running
coordinator (not a mock): the fan_only turn-on/turn-off edges dispatched via real HA state
changes reach _async_thermostat_changed() without raising, without corrupting the routine
comfort-band classification cycle, and without ever routing into a live HVAC-commanding code
path (comfort-band re-arm, thermal-observation start) during the fan_only session itself --
a real (if narrower) regression guard for 'does fan_only session tracking have any command-
level side effect', even though it cannot observe the bookkeeping-level bug this issue was
actually filed for.
The same honest-scoping pattern (naming exactly what a harness limitation prevents proving,
rather than silently claiming broader coverage) is used by
issue_895_sleep_indoor_sensor_swap.json for its own harness-snapshot limitation.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: this scenario's premise (fan_only must never be tracked as
heat/cool runtime, and must never start a thermal observation) matches
docs/thermal-model-v3-spec.md's HVAC observation-type table and the DailyRecord field
documentation added alongside this fix.
(c) Occupant experience: after this fix, a fan-only-only night reports 0 min heat/cool runtime
with its fan-only minutes shown separately and correctly labeled -- never blended into a
number that implies the heater or AC ran, and never triggers a false 'thermal learning
found no observations despite N minutes of HVAC runtime' warning for a night when the
compressor/burner never engaged at all.

events.note: Warm evening, indoor already comfortably within the sleep comfort band (64-72F) -- the routine comfort-band arm has no reason to command cool or heat on its own. Cool outdoor air is available, favorable for a long whole-house-fan / thermostat fan_only run instead of running the compressor.
Normal evening classification: HVAC off recommended -- the compressor/burner is not expected to run at all tonight.

Thermostat (WHF-driven) enters fan_only mode. hvac_action reports 'fan' throughout this session -- never 'heating' or 'cooling' -- exactly the real-world signal pattern behind Issue #912's reported false runtime. This is the real _async_thermostat_changed turn-on edge: session_mode resolves to 'fan_only', _thermostat_fan_only_on_since is armed, and NO thermal (compressor/burner) observation starts.

Fan_only session ends after exactly 400 minutes (22:05 -> 04:45), matching Issue #912's reported ~402-minute magnitude. Compressor/burner never engaged at any point in this window. This is the real turn-off edge: thermostat_fan_only_runtime_minutes banks the full elapsed session, hvac_runtime_minutes is untouched, and _hvac_session_mode resets to None.

assertions.reason: Normal evening classification cycle runs as always.

Issue #912: 'since' is scoped to the moment the fan_only session starts (22:05), deliberately excluding the routine 22:00 classification cycle's own comfort-band threshold command (which legitimately bundles hvac_mode='cool' into a set_temperature call on ANY warm-day cycle per the documented single-setpoint-threshold architecture -- see CLAUDE.md's Warm-Day Classification Behavior section -- and is unrelated to this issue). From the fan_only turn-on edge through the turn-off edge ~400 minutes later, with no further classification cycles firing, production must issue zero additional set_hvac_mode/set_temperature commands into 'cool' or 'heat' -- proving the coordinator's fan_only session-mode tracking (_glide_hvac_session_mode/_start_runtime_timer/_flush_runtime_for_mode) is purely observational bookkeeping with no HVAC-commanding side effect, and that the fan_only turn-on/turn-off edges are never misrouted into the comfort-band re-arm or thermal-observation-start code paths that DO carry live commands.

verdict.summary: A long overnight thermostat fan_only run, driven through the real coordinator's state-change listener, produces zero HVAC-commanding side effects during the session (Issue #912) -- this scenario's scope is deliberately narrower than the full bug fix (see note (a)): it confirms the fan_only session-tracking code path never routes into a live command, but the actual reported defect (hvac_runtime_minutes miscounting fan_only time, and the resulting false thermal_learning_no_observations watchdog) is proven directly by this issue's unit tests, not by this harness scenario.
verdict.observed_behavior: classification_applied at 22:00 (routine comfort-band threshold command, unrelated to this issue) -> thermostat enters fan_only at 22:05 (hvac_action='fan' throughout) -> thermostat returns to off at 04:45 the next morning, 400 minutes later -> zero additional climate.set_hvac_mode/set_temperature calls into 'cool' or 'heat' occur from the fan_only turn-on edge onward.
verdict.expected_behavior: The occupant's activity report shows 0 minutes of heat/cool runtime and the fan-only runtime separately and correctly labeled for this night -- never a false claim that the heater or AC ran, and never a false 'thermal learning found no observations' warning for a night when the compressor/burner never engaged at all. This scenario proves the fan_only session-tracking code path is command-inert; the numeric DailyRecord split and the watchdog's silence are proven directly against the real coordinator by tests/test_hvac_session_detection.py and tests/test_coordinator.py (see note (a)).
